matter_reference_date_basis: Exam session recorded in the candidate matter file as APRIL 2025, giving matter_reference_date 2025-04. Every provision was checked against in_force_from_year and the amendment_events reported by the corpus tool as at that date.
corpus_gaps: No Order made by the Minister under section 3(1) of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 is in the corpus, so the rate of stamp duty on a lease as at April 2025 cannot be established. This is what blocks M024-Q02.
The Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982 is in the corpus only as far as section 71 (Interpretation); no rate schedule was extracted, so it supplies no alternative source for a lease rate.
The Western Province Financial Statute No. 6 of 1990 also charges duty only at the prescribed rate (section 37) and in any event covers the Western Province, whereas the premises here are in Galle.
No fees Order under section 40 of the Notaries Ordinance is in the corpus, so nothing can be said about what a second attesting notary may charge.
Rent and business-tenancy legislation is not in the corpus. This does not affect the two questions annotated, which turn only on execution formalities and stamp duty.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The question asks by what lawful means the lease agreement can be signed. The form required for a lease of immovable property exceeding one month, the notary's duties on execution and attestation, the express statutory recognition of parties who do not sign at the same time and place, and the alternative of signature by a duly authorised attorney are all laid down in the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, the Notaries Ordinance and the Powers of Attorney Ordinance. No judicial authority or Roman-Dutch doctrine is needed to state the permitted modes of execution.

legal_issues.issue: Whether a lease of business premises for two years falls within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and must therefore be executed in notarial form.
Whether both parties must sign the instrument at the same time and place before a single notary, or whether execution may be split.
Whether a notary practising in Colombo may attest the lessor's signature taken in Galle.
Whether the lessor may instead authorise another person to sign the lease on her behalf, and what form that authority must take.

questions.hop_count_basis: Three necessary linked steps across two enactments. Step 1: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 brings a lease longer than one month within the notarial-execution requirement and fixes the form. Step 2: Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (12), read with rule (22) and s.4A, means the executants must sign before a notary who is attesting inside her own judicial zone. Step 3: Notaries Ordinance s.32(2) with s.31 rule (25) permits the parties to sign the one instrument at different times and places before more than one notary. Rule (22) and s.4A are counted inside step 2 as the qualifier that makes step 3 necessary. Verifier: the count stays at three. The power of attorney route and the route under section 2 of the Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance No. 17 of 1852 (PROV-M024-901) are parallel alternatives to the two-notary route, not further links in the chain, and Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (8) (PROV-M024-902) sits inside step 2 as the provision that fixes the number of attesting witnesses. PROV-M024-009 and PROV-M024-010 were moved from supporting to indispensable: on facts where the lessor cannot travel to the notary, the attorney route is one of the answers the question asks for, not background.

enrichment.original_background: Malani Silva is a Notary Practicing in Colombo .Her friend Rupa Perera who is the owner of a business premises in Galle wishes to lease out the same to a Gamini Sirisene for two (02) years at a monthly rental of Rs 150,000/. However Rupa is unable to come to Colombo to sign the Agreement

gold_answer_draft.issue: By what lawful means may a two-year lease of business premises in Galle be signed by a lessor who cannot travel to Colombo and by a lessee dealing with a notary who practises in Colombo?
gold_answer_draft.rule: A lease of immovable property for a period exceeding one month is within Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2, because the only leases excluded are a lease at will and a lease for a period not exceeding one month. Such an instrument has no force in law unless it is in writing and signed by every executant, or by a person duly authorised by the executant, and by the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and is attested by that notary. Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (12) casts the same requirement on the notary as a duty, and rule (22) forbids her from attesting in any area other than that in which she is authorised to practise; s.4A treats the warrant as authorising practice in the judicial zone in which she resides. Notaries Ordinance s.32(2) deals expressly with a deed executed by two or more parties who do not sign it at the same time and place, and s.31 rule (25) governs attestation where an instrument is executed before more than one notary, the notary who first attests complying with the whole of rule (20) and every other notary with paragraphs (a) to (e). Rule (27)(c)(ii) contemplates completion within three months of the first signature. Alternatively, s.2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance allows the instrument to be signed by a person duly authorised by the executant. That authority is a power of attorney within Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.2, which if executed in Sri Lanka must be executed before two witnesses and notarially attested, must satisfy s.3A because the lease is a transaction within s.2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, and must be registered with the Registrar General under s.3; Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (30) then requires the attesting notary to keep a true copy of the power with her protocol and forward a copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
gold_answer_draft.application: The proposed lease runs for two years at Rs 150,000 a month, so it is well outside the one-month exclusion and must be executed notarially. The parties cannot cure Rupa Perera's absence by exchanging the document through the post and signing it apart, because both s.2 and rule (12) require signature in the presence of the notary and of the witnesses, all present together. Malani Silva practises in Colombo, and rule (22) with s.4A stops her from attesting a signature taken in Galle, so she cannot solve the problem by travelling to the lessor. Two routes remain. First, the one instrument may be executed in parts: Rupa Perera signs in Galle with two witnesses before a notary authorised to practise in that zone, and Gamini Sirisene signs in Colombo before Malani Silva, each notary attesting the signatures taken before her. That is the situation s.32(2) addresses, and rule (25) then allocates the attestation, numbering and protocol duties between the two notaries, the notary who first attests complying with the whole of rule (20). Rule (27)(c)(ii) shows the execution is expected to be completed within three months of the first signature. Second, Rupa Perera may grant a power of attorney to a person able to attend in Colombo. Because the lease is a transaction within s.2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, that power must be notarially attested and comply with s.3A of the Powers of Attorney Ordinance, and must be registered with the Registrar General under s.3; the attorney then signs the lease before Malani Silva, who keeps a copy of the power with her protocol under rule (30). The facts do not say whether Rupa Perera is willing to appoint an attorney or whether a notary is readily available in the Galle zone, so the choice between the two routes is practical rather than legal.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The lease must be executed notarially. It may lawfully be signed either by the two parties executing the same instrument at different times and places before two notaries, Rupa Perera before a notary practising in the Galle zone and Gamini Sirisene before Malani Silva in Colombo, as contemplated by Notaries Ordinance s.32(2) and s.31 rule (25); or by Rupa Perera granting a notarially attested and registered power of attorney under the Powers of Attorney Ordinance to an attorney who signs on her behalf in Colombo, as permitted by Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2. What is not open to the parties is signing the agreement outside the presence of a notary and the witnesses, or having the Colombo notary attest a signature taken in Galle.

answer_claims.claim_text: A lease of immovable property for a period exceeding one month falls within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, because the only leases excluded are a lease at will and a lease for a period not exceeding one month.

An instrument within section 2 has no force in law unless it is in writing and signed by every executant, or by a person duly authorised by the executant, and by the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and is attested by that notary.
The notary is under a corresponding duty not to attest unless the executants and the witnesses signed in her presence and in the presence of one another and she signed in their presence.
A notary may not attest a deed in any area other than the area in which she is authorised to practise, that area being the judicial zone in which she resides.
The Notaries Ordinance expressly contemplates a deed executed by two or more parties who do not sign it at the same time and place and provides how the execution rules apply in that case.

Where an instrument is executed before more than one notary, the notary who first attests it must comply with the whole of rule (20) and every other attesting notary with paragraphs (a) to (e) of that rule.

Section 2 also permits the instrument to be signed by a person duly authorised by the executant, and such authority is a power of attorney which, if executed in Sri Lanka, must be executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary public.

A power of attorney granted for a transaction falling within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance must be notarially attested in accordance with the Notaries Ordinance and the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, and every power of attorney must be registered with the Registrar General.
A notary attesting a deed executed through an attorney must keep a true copy of the power of attorney with her protocol and forward a copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.

An instrument executed in parts is expected to be signed by all the parties within three months of the date on which it is first signed by one of them, failing which the notary may be called on to deliver the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
The proposed lease runs for two years, so it is outside the one-month exclusion and must be executed in notarial form.
The parties cannot cure Rupa Perera's inability to travel by exchanging the document and signing it apart from a notary and the witnesses.
Malani Silva, practising in Colombo, cannot attest Rupa Perera's signature in Galle, because that lies outside the judicial zone in which she is authorised to practise.

Rupa Perera may sign the lease in Galle with two witnesses before a notary authorised to practise there while Gamini Sirisene signs the same instrument in Colombo before Malani Silva, each notary attesting the signatures taken before her.

Alternatively Rupa Perera may grant a notarially attested power of attorney complying with section 3A and registered under section 3, and her attorney may then sign the lease in Colombo before Malani Silva.

The agreement can therefore be signed either by both parties executing the one instrument at different times and places before two notaries, or by an attorney signing for Rupa Perera in Colombo under a duly executed and registered power of attorney.
What is not permitted is signature outside the presence of a notary and the witnesses, or attestation by the Colombo notary of a signature taken in Galle.

questions.block_reason: Verifier downgrade. Every provision the researcher cited checks out verbatim and the two routes given are lawful, but the answer presents them as exhaustive. Section 2 of the Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance No. 17 of 1852 (PROV-M024-901, added by the verifier) allows an instrument caught by section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance to be executed instead before a District Judge, or a specially authorised Justice of the Peace, for the district in which the party resides. That makes the conclusion CL-M024-Q01-017 ("what is not permitted is signature outside the presence of a notary and the witnesses") wrong as stated, and CL-M024-Q01-012 and CL-M024-Q01-016 overbroad. CL-M024-Q01-002 also omits the thumb impression requirement in section 2(1)(b), which is part of the signing formality the question asks about, and CL-M024-Q01-013 assumes Malani Silva resides in the Colombo judicial zone when the facts say only that she practises in Colombo. A lawyer must decide whether the 1852 route is still available in practice, and the gold answer prose needs rewriting on that footing before this can be proposed gold.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: Chargeability of a lease to stamp duty, the person liable and the manner of payment are all fixed by the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 and the Notaries Ordinance. No case law or common-law doctrine is needed. The obstacle is not the kind of authority required but that the Act fixes the rate only by Ministerial Order published in the Gazette, and no such Order is in the corpus.

legal_issues.issue: Whether a two-year lease of business premises is an instrument chargeable with stamp duty.
What rate of stamp duty applies to a lease and on what base the duty is calculated.
Who is liable to pay the duty and how and when it must be paid.

questions.hop_count_basis: Two necessary steps. Section 4(i) of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act classifies a lease of property as a specified instrument, and section 3(1) charges duty on every specified instrument at the rate the Minister determines by Order published in the Gazette. The third step, applying that rate to the rent reserved, cannot be taken because the Order lies outside the corpus.

enrichment.original_background: Malani Silva is a Notary Practicing in Colombo .Her friend Rupa Perera who is the owner of a business premises in Galle wishes to lease out the same to a Gamini Sirisene for two (02) years at a monthly rental of Rs 150,000/. However Rupa is unable to come to Colombo to sign the Agreement

gold_answer_draft.issue: What value of stamp duty is payable on a two-year lease of business premises at a monthly rent of Rs 150,000, and who must pay it?
gold_answer_draft.rule: Section 4 of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 lists a lease or hire of any property as a specified instrument. Section 3(1) charges stamp duty on every specified instrument executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette, and section 3(2) allows different rates for different classes of instrument. Section 6(c) makes the duty on a lease payable by the lessee unless there is an agreement to the contrary. Section 8(2) allows the duty on a lease of immovable property to be paid to a prescribed bank before or at the time of execution, with the bank certificate affixed to the instrument. Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (6) forbids the notary from attesting unless she has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided, and rule (7)(a) and (b) require the notary to pay the duty and to affix the stamps or the bank receipt to the duplicate.
gold_answer_draft.application: The subject of the agreement is business premises, so the instrument is a lease of property and a specified instrument, and it is to be executed in Sri Lanka, so duty is chargeable on it. The rent reserved is Rs 150,000 a month for two years. The Act itself states no rate: section 3(1) leaves the rate to a Ministerial Order published in the Gazette, and no such Order is in the corpus consulted for this map, nor was any rate schedule extracted from the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982. The rate applicable to a lease in April 2025, and the base on which it is charged, therefore cannot be established from the available statutes, and the money figure cannot be computed without importing a rate from outside the corpus. Subject to that, the duty falls on Gamini Sirisene as lessee unless the parties agree otherwise, it may be paid to a prescribed bank before or at execution, and Malani Silva must not attest until she is satisfied that the duty is provided.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The lease is a specified instrument chargeable with stamp duty and, absent agreement to the contrary, the lessee Gamini Sirisene bears the duty, payable to a prescribed bank before or at the time of execution. The value of the duty cannot be stated from the corpus, because the rate is fixed by a Ministerial Order under section 3(1) of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act which is not among the extracted sources. The question is therefore blocked for want of the rate-fixing instrument.

answer_claims.claim_text: A lease or hire of any property is a specified instrument for the purposes of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act.
Stamp duty is charged on every specified instrument executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka at such rate as the Minister determines by Order published in the Gazette.
In the case of a lease the duty is payable by the lessee unless there is an agreement to the contrary.
Duty on a lease of immovable property may be paid to a prescribed bank before or at the time of execution of the instrument.
The notary must not attest unless she has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided, and must pay the duty and affix the stamps or the bank receipt to the duplicate.
The proposed two-year lease of business premises at Rs 150,000 a month is a specified instrument chargeable with stamp duty.
Absent agreement to the contrary the duty falls on Gamini Sirisene as lessee.

questions.block_reason: The rate of stamp duty on a lease is not in the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 itself. Section 3(1) fixes it by Ministerial Order published in the Gazette, and no such rate Order, and no rate schedule under the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982, is present in the frozen corpus. Chargeability, the person liable and the manner of payment can all be established, but the money value the question asks for cannot be given without quoting a rate from outside the corpus. Verifier: the block is confirmed. Section 3(1) fixes the rate only by Ministerial Order, section 5 leaves exemptions to the same mechanism, and section 13 carries over no rate from Act No. 43 of 1982; a grep of 43-1982 for "lease" returns only sections 19, 24 and 46 and no rate schedule. Everything else the answer states is verified: chargeability under section 4(i), the lessee's liability under section 6(c), payment to a prescribed bank under section 8(2), and the notary's duties under section 31 rules (6) and (7). The term "prescribed bank" is itself defined nowhere in the corpus, a further gap on the manner of payment.
